name: Putinism
summary: Putinism is the loose governing outlook of Vladimir Putin's Russia, which scholars describe as a strong centralised state, great-power status, sovereignty against the West and conservative Orthodox values. Putin's own interviews and the CSIS report give positions on democracy abroad, privatization, nuclear deterrence, family, patriotic education and the Church, but little on most economic or constitutional questions.
scope: Putinism as the scholars who name it (Migranyan, Glinski, Aron, Snegovaya and colleagues) describe it, and Putin's own words in his interviews with Oliver Stone and his 2021 essay. Putin denies Russia has a state ideology, so only positions stated by him or described by those scholars are answered; policy inferred from Wikipedia summaries is not.
